note: Braids has exactly two knobs here: parameter_[0] (p1, TIMBRE) is the symbol rate (digital_oscillator.cc:2192-2193, pitch_ - 1536 + ((parameter_[0]-32767)>>3); parameter_[0] is CONSTRAIN(...,0,32767) in braids.cc:223 -- not the full int16 range -- so the term is always <= 0 and the note only ever moves DOWN from the octave-down centre, matching kDigitalModulationSymbolOffset/-Range). p2 (COLOR) is parameter_[1], the payload byte the packet's one-pole filter chases (digital_oscillator.cc:2217-2219, filter_state=(filter_state*3+parameter_[1])>>2, data_byte=filter_state>>7; sign of the port's kDigitalModulationPayloadPole=0.75). HARMONICS (frame length) and MORPH (symbol-transition shaping) are new -- Braids' frame is hardwired to 1088 symbols (digital_oscillator.cc:2207, 64+4*256) and its constellation switches are always hard steps -- so every case pins them to the values that collapse the port back onto exactly what Braids does: HARMONICS=1.0 (the engine's own header/README: 'HARMONICS = 1 is still Braids' 1,088 exactly') and MORPH=0.0 (hard steps, no glide). Those are NOT noon/0.5 like a typical spare macro -- 0.5 is a sound Braids cannot make (a 187-symbol frame with no frame-length knob to reach it), so pinning to 0.5 here would be the same class of mistake the fourth-macro convention exists to avoid, just aimed the other way. TIMBRE and MACRO get both-ends coverage below (payload-low/-high, timbre-low/-high); HARMONICS/MORPH do not, by the same logic that keeps them off csaw/fold's swept axes -- moving them is a sound Braids cannot make at all, not just a corner of one it can.  Cents tolerance is dropped from every case except pitch-check: ab_compare.autocorrelation_f0 carries a real, non-trivial, note-dependent bias at these notes -- verified directly by feeding it a mathematically exact synthetic sine (no engine involved): a pure 110.000 Hz tone at this harness's own window size (rate*0.25 = 12000 samples, i.e. ~27.5 cycles at 110 Hz) measures back at 110.294 Hz (+4.6 cents), while 220 Hz and 440 Hz measure back within 0.002 cents. TIMBRE and COLOR/MACRO both need a slow-enough symbol rate to keep the preamble/sync/payload regions inside a render of a few seconds, which pins these cases to low notes (36-45) where the estimator is demonstrably unreliable -- so pitch-check exists purely to give one case a note (A4) and a short, preamble-only window where the estimator is trustworthy, and it passes. Direct math (ComputePhaseIncrement against braids/resources.cc's lut_oscillator_increments, and NoteToFrequency against kCorrectedSampleRate) confirms the carrier itself is correct well beyond 1 cent at every note used here -- see the DSP-mapping doc alongside this file.
